details: This package republishes the WhatsApp Web library Baileys under the @alannxds scope while its README, badges and LICENSE reference the canonical @whiskeysockets/baileys project, so installers get a look-alike name instead of the upstream package. Its manifest declares cache-manager ^7.2.8, a range that resolves to cache-manager 7.2.10, the compromised release of that package, so a normal install pulls the malicious code in as a transitive dependency. Importing the module entry point lib/index.js unconditionally requests hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/alannzxd/xclient/refs/heads/main/information[.]json — a repository controlled by the fork's author, not by any Baileys upstream — and prints the response to the console together with a Telegram contact (t[.]me/alannxd). This package is a republished fork of the WhatsApp Web library Baileys published under the @alannxds scope while its README, badges and LICENSE reference the canonical @whiskeysockets/baileys project, so installers get a look-alike name rather than the upstream package. Its dependency manifest declares cache-manager ^7.2.8, a range that resolves to cache-manager 7.2.10 — the compromised release of that package — so a normal install pulls the malicious code in as a transitive dependency. The package also carries a preinstall hook (node./engine-requirements.js, which only checks the Node major version), and importing the module entry point lib/index.js immediately performs an outbound request to hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/alannzxd/xclient/refs/heads/main/information[.]json, a repository controlled by the fork's author rather than any Baileys upstream, and prints the returned content to the console while advertising a Telegram contact (t[.]me/alannxd) and a WhatsApp channel. The library code bundles the full Baileys protocol stack plus extra message helpers in lib/Socket/luxu.js that stamp messages with a hardcoded forwarded-newsletter identity (newsletterJid "0@newsletter", newsletterName "WhatsApp", senderName "AlannXD", forwardingScore 99999), making relayed messages appear to originate from a WhatsApp update card.
